assumptions.condition: \(\forall r\in\mathcal R\setminus\{0\},\ \forall i\in N,\quad i\in J_r\ \lor\ \operatorname{Pa}(i)\subseteq J_r.\)

novel.justification: Coordinated perturbation screens and multi-component policy pilots can shift every direct input of an exposed response while assigning all manipulated coordinates their shifted natural values.

definitions.name: parent natural-value shift regime
definitions.construction: For \(r\in\mathcal R\setminus\{0\}\), draw \((X,U)\) from \(M\), assign \(X_j^{\sigma_r}=X_j+\eta_{rj}\) for every \(j\in J_r\), retain the same \(U\), and recursively evaluate every node in \(N\setminus J_r\) in a topological order of \(G\); the resulting full law is \(P_r\).

definitions.name: observed shift experiment
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal D_{\Delta}(M)=(P_r)_{r\in\mathcal R}\), where \(P_0\) is observational and every \(P_r\), \(r\ne0\), is generated by \(\sigma_r\).

definitions.name: exact soft shift-rank cover
definitions.construction: \(\{(S_i,K_i,\Delta_i):i\in N,\ p_i>0\}:\quad C_{\Delta}=1\Longleftrightarrow\forall i\in N\text{ with }p_i>0,\ \ker(\mathcal L_i)=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf 1_{K_i}\}.\)

definitions.name: normalized mechanism inverse
definitions.construction: Solve \(\mathcal L_i f_i^{\mathcal D}=g_i\) in \(C(K_i)\), then select the solution satisfying \(\mathbb E_{P_0}[X_i-f_i^{\mathcal D}(X_{\operatorname{Pa}(i)})]=0\); for \(p_i=0\), set \(f_i^{\mathcal D}=\mathbb E_{P_0}[X_i]\).

definitions.name: spectral shift-design handle
definitions.construction: Use the Dirichlet form generated by \(\mathcal L_i\), its first nonzero singular value on mean-zero functions, and overlap-graph discretizations of \(S_i\) to design a budget-constrained \(\Delta_i\) and a stable inverse for \(f_i^{\mathcal D}\).

statements.statement: For every \(M\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{shift}}(G,K)\), every \(i\in N\) with \(p_i>0\), every \(\delta\in\Delta_i\), and every \(q\in S_i\), the observed regime regressions obey \(m_{i,\delta}(q+\delta)-m_{i,0}(q)=f_i(q+\delta)-f_i(q)\); equivalently, \(g_i=\mathcal L_i f_i\).
statements.justification: The identity removes the unknown confounding regression without Gaussian conditional-expectation algebra.
statements.gap: Sani, Lee, and Shpitser identify shift counterfactuals graphically, but do not use cross-regime shifts to cancel an arbitrary dependent additive disturbance regression.
statements.consumer: The identity converts full regime laws into a deterministic inverse problem for each nonlinear mechanism.

statements.statement: The data map \(M\mapsto\mathcal D_{\Delta}(M)\) identifies \((f,\mu_U,(P^{\operatorname{do}(X_A=a)})_{A,a})\) on \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{shift}}(G,K)\), for every \((A,a)\) whose recursive parent values remain in \(K\), if and only if \(C_{\Delta}=1\). When \(C_{\Delta}=1\), the identifying functional is \(f=f^{\mathcal D}\), \(\mu_U=\mu_U^{\mathcal D}\), and \(P^{\operatorname{do}(X_A=a)}=(T_{A,a}^{f^{\mathcal D}})_{\#}\mu_U^{\mathcal D}\). If \(C_{\Delta}=0\) at node \(i\), select a nonconstant \(c\in\ker(\mathcal L_i)\) with observational mean zero. There exist two bounded non-Gaussian SCMs that agree on the complete tuple \(\mathcal D_{\Delta}\) and differ on a hard intervention at a parent value in \(K_i\): one has \(f_i^{(0)}=0\) and \(U_i^{(0)}=W\), while the other has \(f_i^{(1)}=\varepsilon c\) and \(U_i^{(1)}=W-\varepsilon c(X_{\operatorname{Pa}(i)})\) for a sufficiently small \(\varepsilon>0\), with all remaining mechanisms chosen identically.
statements.justification: This is an exact design frontier for recovering every intervention law from finite soft-shift experiments under unrestricted dependent non-Gaussian disturbances.
statements.gap: Elahi, Ghasemi, and Kocaoglu give an exact hard parent-intervention cover only for Gaussian average outcomes; Correa and Bareinboim give graphical soft-intervention calculi without an additive-mechanism rank frontier or residual-law recovery.
statements.consumer: Policy experiments that nudge natural doses or prices can be audited for universal full-law identifiability before data collection.

statements.statement: For any nontrivial \(G\) admitting a bounded parent support, neither \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{shift}}(G,K)\subseteq\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{EGK}}(G)\) nor \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{EGK}}(G)\subseteq\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{shift}}(G,K)\): bounded non-Gaussian dependent disturbances witness the first failure, and nondegenerate Gaussian parent disturbances with unbounded support witness the second.
statements.justification: The class relation prevents the soft-shift result from being misreported as a formal extension on the same model class.
statements.gap: The closest hard-cover theorem and the present shift theorem impose different disturbance and support restrictions whose relation is otherwise easy to obscure.
statements.consumer: Referees and applied users obtain an explicit boundary for transferring conclusions between the two designs.

statements.statement: If \(U_1,\ldots,U_d\) are mutually independent, then \(m_{i,0}(q)=f_i(q)\) for every nonroot node after the centered normalization, so \(P_0\) alone identifies \(f\), \(\mu_U\), and every \(P^{\operatorname{do}(X_A=a)}\) by the ordinary additive-noise residual pushforward, without requiring \(C_{\Delta}=1\).
statements.justification: The reduction is the required sanity check against the standard causally sufficient additive-noise model.
statements.gap: Peters, Mooij, Janzing, and Schölkopf use independent disturbances; the new rank condition is needed only to cancel parent-dependent disturbance regressions created by confounding.
statements.consumer: Existing additive-noise analyses become a transparent special case of the identification functional.

statements.statement: Using \(\mathsf H_{\star}\), characterize and construct, for a budget \(b\), a family \(\Delta\) with at most \(b\) shifts per node that yields injectivity and the largest attainable stability modulus for recovering \(f^{\mathcal D}\) when each implemented shift law lies in a shrinking neighborhood of its nominal \(P_r\); establish a matching minimax lower bound over the same primitive neighborhood.
statements.justification: Exact injectivity alone does not determine which feasible soft-shift design remains informative under small implementation errors.
statements.gap: Correa and Bareinboim characterize graphical computability, while invariant-prediction and shift-intervention work do not optimize the spectral conditioning of a confounded-ANM mechanism inverse.
statements.consumer: Experimenters choosing a small number of dose or price nudges obtain a design criterion with a certified robustness margin.

sampling_model.design: A finite known collection of parent-complete natural-value shifts \(\sigma_r\), together with the observational regime.
sampling_model.units: Independent units are sampled within each regime; the population identification theorem takes every regime law as known.
sampling_model.treatment: Regime \(\sigma_r\) assigns \(X_j+\eta_{rj}\) to every \(j\in J_r\), preserves the same exogenous vector, and leaves each unshifted node exposed only when all of its parents belong to \(J_r\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every shifted support \(S_i+\delta\) lies in \(K_i\); the exact global requirement is \(\ker(\mathcal L_i)=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf 1_{K_i}\}\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No finite-sample rate is claimed in the exact-identification theorem; stable estimation under approximate shifts is isolated in \(\text{oeq:stable-minimal-shift-design}\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: All Gaussian average outcomes are identifiable exactly when supplied hard regimes expose every node while intervening on all of its parents.
The \(\sigma\)-calculus and its algorithm are sound for identifying stochastic interventions and for surrogate-experiment identification.
The \(\sigma\)-calculus is complete for soft transportability across domains.
Shift interventions on natural treatment values and recursive shift policies admit graphical identification algorithms, with estimation for a special mean target.
Soft-intervention invariances characterize latent-variable interventional graph equivalence and yield additional orientation rules.
Continuous additive-noise models identify the causal graph under independent-error regularity conditions.

tldr: Known soft interventions that translate a node's natural parent vector reveal differences of its structural function while exactly cancelling an arbitrary parent-dependent disturbance regression. The proposal proves that all mechanisms, the complete joint residual law, every hard-intervention distribution, and every bounded analysis of interest are identified if and only if the induced translation-difference operator has only constants in its kernel. Failure of this rank cover yields two bounded non-Gaussian SCMs, built with a four-point Rademacher residual, that agree on the entire observational-plus-shift tuple but disagree under a hard intervention.

project_justification.gap: Published confounded additive-noise cover results use surgical parent interventions and Gaussian disturbances, while graphical soft-intervention results do not exploit additive structure to recover mechanisms or a dependent residual law.
project_justification.niche: Natural-value shift experiments preserve heterogeneous baseline variation and create observable within-mechanism increments even when latent confounding makes every observational regression biased.
project_justification.fill: The shift-difference null space supplies an exact necessary-and-sufficient design criterion, an explicit residual-pushforward functional, and a matching bounded non-Gaussian indistinguishability construction.

related_work: Elahi, Ghasemi, and Kocaoglu establish a necessary-and-sufficient hard-intervention cover for average outcomes under multivariate Gaussian disturbances; their result motivates the cover question but not the shift-difference operator. Correa and Bareinboim develop the \(\sigma\)-calculus and completeness theory for stochastic interventions and soft transportability in unrestricted graphical models; the present kernel is informed by their intervention semantics but targets additive-mechanism recovery. Sani, Lee, and Shpitser distinguish shifts of natural treatment values from recursively defined shift policies and give graphical identification and estimation results; their natural-value semantics supplies the intervention object used here. Kocaoglu, Jaber, Shanmugam, and Bareinboim characterize graph equivalence from soft environments with latent variables; they target structure rather than full effect-law recovery. Peters, Mooij, Janzing, and Schölkopf identify additive-noise graphs under independent disturbances; the independent-noise proposition records the corresponding no-confounding reduction.
technical_internal_limitation: The natural-value shift law is a cross-world intervention that preserves each unit's baseline parent vector. A mechanism-changing environment that merely shifts a parent marginal, without this correspondence, need not satisfy the contrast identity. This distinction is part of the design semantics and is not a conclusion about arbitrary soft interventions.
honest_scope: The settled target is population exact identification for a known DAG, compact parent domains, continuous mechanisms, continuous conditional disturbance means, and exactly implemented natural-value shifts. The rank condition is nonvacuous: on a one-dimensional interval, two overlapping shifts with an irrational ratio force every continuous common invariant to be constant. The theorem does not claim graph recovery, clinical effects, or finite-sample inference. The optimal stable design under approximate shift implementation is explicitly open. Under mutually independent disturbances, the construction reduces to ordinary observational additive-noise recovery.

seed_details.rationale: The hard parent-fixing full-law route exhausted its review cursor.
Its theorem-level contribution is primarily statistical and does not match the required exact-identification cluster.
It reuses the exhausted mechanism-and-residual recovery step and is therefore not a sufficiently structural pivot.
Its natural contribution is partial identification rather than exact identification.
Known natural-value shifts yield observable structural increments, and a functional rank condition can be both sufficient and universally necessary under arbitrary dependent disturbances.
Joint graph recovery remains viable but requires an additional orientation condition not needed for the known-graph shift kernel.
The design problem is retained as a consumer of the shift-rank theorem rather than the first theorem-level kernel.
Approximate cover is retained as the stability question after exact rank is characterized.

literature_map.settled: Hard regimes that leave a node free while intervening on all of its parents are necessary and sufficient for all Gaussian average outcomes in the published model.
literature_map.open_boundary: The published theorem does not cover natural-value shifts, arbitrary dependent Borel disturbances, or complete intervention laws.

literature_map.settled: The \(\sigma\)-calculus supplies sound identification rules for stochastic interventions and is complete for soft transportability.
literature_map.open_boundary: No located result converts natural-value shift contrasts into an exact functional rank frontier for confounded additive mechanisms.

literature_map.settled: Shift interventions on the treated and shift interventions as policies have formal counterfactual semantics and graphical identification algorithms.
literature_map.open_boundary: The located shift literature does not use multiple supplied shift laws to identify an arbitrarily confounded additive mechanism and its joint residual distribution.

literature_map.settled: Soft-environment invariances characterize interventional graph equivalence with latent variables and support orientation rules.
literature_map.open_boundary: Graph equivalence does not provide an identifying functional for nonlinear mechanisms or hard-intervention distributions under dependent noise.

novelty_justification: The closest result of Elahi, Ghasemi, and Kocaoglu characterizes hard parent covers for Gaussian average outcomes. The closest soft-intervention identification theory of Correa and Bareinboim gives graphical calculi for stochastic policies and transportability. Neither result states a functional rank condition under which finitely many natural-value shifts recover nonlinear additive mechanisms, the complete dependent disturbance law, and all hard-intervention distributions, nor supplies a same-regime-tuple bounded witness when that rank fails.
